title: A lot has happened
text: “Getting back to the topic at hand—the Colosseum, huh… I’ve been here before, but it’s always bustling.”
“What’s this? Are you entering the Perfect Hide Justice tournament?”
“…Ren, if we entered, it wouldn’t even be a contest.”

“True… I thought we could use it to raise funds for reconstruction, but using a hero’s power in the Colosseum feels a bit off. Still, we don’t really want to rely too much on money from other countries, do we?”
“Rival, you won’t make any money in this world by filming skits based on Takt, you know?”
“I know that, of course.”

Hmph. Rival, it’s a shame that in this loop, I can’t torment Takt the way I did in that previous loop. I wanted to make him suffer more, but it’s a pity he’s already been ‘shipped’ in this loop. Since we can’t film, that means we can’t use the gags Rival planned, you see.
“Since you two are looping, you could make money by hitting the jackpot on horse racing tickets or in Filolial races…”
“We’re the kind of people who don’t need to do that.”
“That’s right.”
Hmm? It seems Ren and Itsuki have just accepted that on their own. Ren and Itsuki in this world are surprisingly obedient in strange ways, after all.
“Oh? Who’s that over there…? Hey!”
Just as we were talking, the old man from the weapon shop was waving at us from over there. What an unusual place to run into him. If I recall correctly, in this world…
“Isn’t that An-chan, the hero, and her friends over there?”
“The old man from the weapon shop!”
Ren and Itsuki replied to the old man from the weapon shop.
“Long time no see.”
Perhaps because my Father knew him, he greeted him as well.
“I heard all about it. So you finally saved the world from the threat of the Waves, huh? I was a little worried when you first came to my shop, but you really pulled it off.”
“No, no…”

“Honestly, I was surprised. First, rumors spread just like ‘Shield-An’ said, and right after that, word got out that the heroes had all run away. Then there were even rumors that the Wise King of Wisdom had been killed by the heroes. On top of that, public order kept getting worse and worse—it was a total mess.”
“Um… I’m sorry. It’s our fault.”
For some reason, Itsuki is apologizing. That’s not something you should be apologizing for, is it? The Trash of this world tried to kill us, after all. It’s just karma.
“After that, when I went to your shop, it was closed, so I thought I’d caused you some trouble…”

“You’re not going to get in trouble just for selling some weapons. It was more because of the decline in public safety. We just kept getting weird customers day after day, so we closed up shop and hit the road—that’s all.”
“Is that so…”
“Well, what really surprised me was hearing about that huge incident that happened in Melromarc afterward. I heard the Hero, An-chan, and the others took care of it, right?”
The Ghost Crimson Swine Incident, huh? It’s like Melromarc’s “before and after.” That incident caused a massive amount of damage. But we were the ones who resolved it, you know.
“Yeah, we managed to defeat them somehow. Apparently, that country’s first princess was involved with the mastermind behind the Wave—I guess you could say she revealed her true colors.”
“I’ve heard rumors about that, too. So, you guys put an end to the Wave in the end, right? I’m pretty proud to say I helped out, too.”

Rin and Itsuki are chatting away like that. On the other hand, my father is watching that exchange from a step back. In my memory, I have the impression that the guy from the weapon shop talks with my father quite often.
“Father, is it okay if I don’t talk to the guy from the weapon shop?”
“Huh? Well… I’ve talked to him before, but it’s just at the level of, ‘Oh, that’s the guy from the shop where I bought my chain mail.’”

Hmm… It’s true that in this loop, my Father doesn’t have much of a relationship with the guy at the weapon shop. Since Ren and Itsuki checked the evidence and such, it must have left an impression on them.
“He’s quite skilled, and he’s someone my Father from the first world trusts.”
“Ah, so he really is a man of integrity, then. He seemed generous, too.”
“That’s An-chan with the shield over there. You’ve been through a lot, haven’t you, An-chan?”
“Yeah.”
As Father answers, the weapons shop owner stares intently at him and tilts his head.

“…I don’t know how to put it, but An-chan, haven’t you changed since I last saw you? It’s not like… the young, carefree, cocky vibe you had before—you seem more pure-hearted, or maybe just more honest now.”
“I can’t deny that.”
“That’s true. Naofumi was a lot more of a joker back when we first met.”
“You know…”
My Father scratched his head with a crinkle, looking exasperated.
“It’s just that since everyone’s been looking out for me, I’m trying not to push things too far.”
“The kinder you are to my Father, the kinder he becomes!”
“Well, that’s true. And I know that Naofumi-san is scary when he gets angry.”
“Though sometimes I wonder if I was born the wrong gender.”
“That’s why, both of you…”
As my Father furrowed his brow, Kou, who was standing a little ways away, flinched and jerked back sharply. Hmm… Kou has become quite a nervous kid, hasn’t he?
“It’s enviable how well two heroes get along.”
“Aren’t you going back to the shop, Dad?”
“Hmm… I guess it’s about time I went back. How’s Melromarc doing these days?”
“It’s gradually recovering. It’s true that the ghost of that princess caused massive damage, but the buildings themselves didn’t suffer that much.”
“Why don’t you guys come join us where we’re working on the reconstruction right now? If possible, I’d like you to teach me blacksmithing.”
Ren is making some kind of proposal.
“Oh? An-chan the Swordsman is interested in blacksmithing?”
“Yeah… I want to learn a skill other than fighting.”
Ren, having adjusted his thick-rimmed glasses, glances once at Itsuki, me, and my Father before saying to my dad. He learned this in his first world by apprenticing under a master.
“What kind of reason is that?”
“A Sword Hero can’t just be good at fighting.”
“I don’t really get it, but…”
“Ren doesn’t have any standout skills among us. That’s why he wants to learn blacksmithing, which he’s interested in.”
“Skills, huh… Do you guys have anything you’re good at?”
My dad asks Itsuki.

“It seems I have a talent for playing musical instruments. It still doesn’t quite feel right to me, but that’s what they say. And Motoyasu is quite versatile—he’s good at sewing and all sorts of things.”
“What about An, the Shield?”
“He’s got the makings of a great homemaker. Any domestic woman would run away barefoot in his presence.”
“Itsuki? I’m starting to think about ripping those headphones right off your head. Sooner or later, someone’s actually going to steal them from you.”
Itsuki’s still as sharp-tongued as ever. That was way more than necessary.
“My Father is just very affectionate!”
“Motoyasu, just keep quiet.”
“Wait, you guys with the swords and bows… why are you wearing such weird gear?”
“We’ve been through a lot.”
“It’s all a precaution. We can’t afford to get ‘awakened.’”
“I don’t really get it, but looks like even heroes have their share of troubles.”
The old man crosses his arms and looks at us again.
“If you want, I can send you to Melromarc on the way back. Since you’re a hero, you can get there in an instant.”
“Oh? That’d be a big help.”
“While I’m at it, should I introduce you to my fellow apprentice, the Mole?”
I’m pretty sure the Mole’s uncle had come to the village as well. I can introduce him to the guy at the weapon shop.
“Mole…”
“He’s a member of the Rumo clan.”
“If he’s from the Rumo clan and my fellow apprentice, does that mean it’s Torii?”
“No, wait a second, Motoyasu. Is there a master blacksmith in the Rumo clan!?”
Ren asked me and my Rival at this point.
“It’s Mole the Blacksmith, Mole’s uncle.”
“Imiya’s uncle!? Isn’t he the hardware store owner!?”
“Huh? Um… My uncle makes tools for everyone. I figured he must know a thing or two…”
So that’s what a hardware store is, then.
“In our world, I think hardware store owners are usually former blacksmiths who switched careers, right?”
“I see. So there were other people we could turn to.”
“According to Blacksmith Mole, he didn’t really undergo that much formal training? He just makes all kinds of things together with the old man at the weapon shop.”
“If I can meet Torii, I’m fine with going back. I didn’t achieve the goal of my journey, but if that’s the case, it’s no problem.”
“The purpose of the journey?”
“Ah, well, I’ve actually been looking for someone. I’m searching for my master, but I can’t find him.”
It seems the old man at the weapons shop has some kind of master. He’s been traveling around looking for that master, apparently.
“Should we help look for him? Do you know anything, Motoyasu-kun or Gaelion-chan?”
“I don’t know. I’ve never heard of him, not even in the loop.”
“I don’t know either.”
“Even someone who’s been through the Loop can’t find him…”
“I wonder where he is.”

“It’s just a ‘nice to find’ sort of thing—don’t worry about it too much. Torii, well, I think metalwork suits you better for the times ahead. An-chan the Swordsman—even if you learn blacksmithing, it won’t make you that much money, but are you okay with that?”
Ren nods in response to the weapon shop owner’s question.
“Yeah, if possible, I’d like to just quietly forge weapons. Without making a big show of it.”
“You sure do say things in a way that makes me wonder, Sword-Wielding An. How good are you, anyway?”
“I know the basics of weapon crafting…”
“Well, you’ll have to learn all sorts of things, not just mass-produce weapons.”
“Of course! I’ll see it through so I’m every bit as good as any Sword Hero!”

At that moment, I’m sure I, Itsuki, and my Father all thought to ourselves: Ren’s outstanding talent must surely lie in becoming a Dark Holy Hero alongside Black Thunder. In terms of aptitude, there’s no doubt he possesses extraordinary talent. Anyway, Ren will now officially begin his blacksmithing apprenticeship, and the weapon shop owner will return to Melromarc.
Just as we were talking, cheers rang out from the direction of the arena. The match must have concluded.
“Oh, looks like we missed the match. Instead of talking here, why don’t we head over to the stands?”
“Yeah, you’re right. Let’s at least go watch it.”
Panda seems to be getting restless, too. So, we decided to go watch the match at the Colosseum.
“Since it’s a match featuring a famous fighter from Zeltoble, the spectators are really hyped up…”
“A little while ago, the people at the Colosseum were trying to convince Sasa-chan to enter the match, weren’t they?”
“They said they were having trouble putting together a match worth watching now that you and I aren’t fighting anymore. I guess there aren’t any other tough opponents left.”
After all, we’d recruited Big Sister and Panda and left Zeltoble. Panda was told something similar during her lap with my Father, who’d devoted himself to our Rival.
“I wonder if there just aren’t enough kids who put on exciting matches? Big Sister, I really enjoy fighting Sasa-chan—it’s so much fun!”
“I know that putting on a show is important, of course.”

Panda’s fights are certainly flashy. Big Sister’s older sister is just plain strong, but I get the feeling her matches are the kind that really put on a show, too. I ran wild in Zeltoble as the Filolial Mask myself, after all. My spectacular performance really livened up the matches.
“Why not just have the heroes step into the ring wearing masks, then?”
Just as we arrived at the spectator seats in the Colosseum…
“Ah! Look at that!”
I let out a cry when I saw the fighter currently in the Colosseum!
“Oh?”
“Whoa—so that was his match?”
I pointed at the fighter who was posing as the victor.
“Father, that’s a great Elephant!”　He’s an Elephant who’s good friends with Kou!”
“Wooooah!” The Elephant, known as the Queen of Earthquakes, was performing her victory routine, and the arena was buzzing with excitement.
“Motoyasu-kun…”
My Father gave me a look of exasperation. What’s the matter?
“Is that supposed to be a joke?”
“Isn’t he being serious? I mean, he says that all the time, so it doesn’t sound strange at all.”
“If you want to cheer up Kou, the Spear Hero, you should go talk to him.”

I’m not happy with my Rival’s words, but I look over at Kou. It’s true—he’s been following us along very quietly. This quietness is almost painful to watch! Kou, just wait a sec! I’ll bring Elephant—who’s really good friends with you—over here.
“I’ll talk to him even without being told. Wait for me! Elephant—”
“I’m going too!”
“Ah! Motoyasu-kun! Wait, why’s Lars-chan here too!?”

As I ran around to catch up with Elephant, who was leaving the arena, and headed toward the reception desk, Panda followed along for some reason. So, when I went to the counter to collect my prize money, I found Elephant, who had just finished his match, strolling over to the counter to collect his prize. Since it’s an outdoor colosseum, the prize money’s on the low side. But it’s safer that way. And they pay out the rewards quickly, too.
“Hey, Elmelo!”
Before I could even call out, Panda called out to Elephant.
“Larsa?”
Elephant turned around at the sound of Panda’s voice and looked at both of us.
“Long time no see. Were you back in Zeltoble?”
“Yeah. Well, I guess I just came here to take a break.”
“I see… Haven’t you gotten a little rounder, you? Like… physically?”
Not only does she eat the meals Father cooks, but she’s also already carrying his child. She does seem a bit rounder than before.
